paragraphs: My name is Bea, I'm a visually impaired trans woman based in Manchester. I have many creative purseiuts including photography, music, art ect.

I don't like taliing about this out of the blue but I will put it here to point to. Does being visually impaired and photography make sense together? In my opnion in makes perfect sense and I'd argue you've missed an important reason of why people do photography and to me it falls into the same area as people who complain about modern art not being of anything meaning they expect a painting or a sculpure to be a realistic replication of the real world and the quality of the art is equal to it's realism. However, that misses the whole point of being alive which is to explore your surroundings, figure out how things work, and use that knowledge to transform the world around you. Taking the sharpest, most compositoinally perfect and realistic photo is one pursuit but what does that tell you about the world, the subject or the photographer? That maybe they spent years pefecting their technique, that they might be extremely gifted at what they do, that they have access to the latest gear, that they have access to amazing locations. Which as we live in a comercialy focused society a comercially attractie approach wins out. But I beleive in art and specifically making art being egaliterian. I take photos so that I can learn a bit more about mysqlf, what does my brain and eyes pick out of the surrounds as meaningful, to learn how I, my body and being interact with a camera and photos. Maybe I can't tell what is acutally in focus when i take a photo but can things still look good out of focus? Maybe I don't see the finest details but does that matter if I can find beauty in the braoder form of a subject.
Some of the things I've learnt about myself:
I really like the colour yellow I think there's meant to be scientific rasons for that and I should look it up.

I seem to often pick cranes out. I'm not sure why, if it's their bright colouring against a desaturated city, or that I can know where they are at night because of the red lights on them. Or if they surround an area of blank sky as the skyline is still being constructed.
Colour can be more important than form, I will farm more easily pick out a subject if they are brihglty coloured compared to their surroundings. Or just in good contrast.

Abstraction, to me the world is more abstract than to others with my imagination filling in the gaps. Sometimes skyscrapers look like crystal structures like a quarz crytstal. Larger blocks and busy skylines feel like big cliffs or a canyon. If it's night and it has rained the refelction of traffic lights, headlights form a psychadelic world of glowing shapes without form. People disapear into the night and I can have time to myself even in a busy city

My closing thought would be that anything we do is about exploring our senses. We cook so that we can taste, we make music so we can hear ect. I'm sure there's highly uliterian people who only eat for fuel but I don't think I'm anything close to that.
